lines: Map jokes are easy to <wavy>fold badly</wavy>.
Mapping jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with parchment on them.
I keep a spare joke near the map table. It is not always ready for public use.
I told a joke at the map table once. The workstation took it better than the villagers did.
People say I work too much. I say the work is the only one here that listens.
If confidence could be traded, this village would be rich and still somehow underprepared.
I tried taking a day off. The village immediately treated it like an emergency drill.
A good joke needs timing. Around here, timing usually trips over a chicken.
I would laugh louder, but someone would ask me to explain it and ruin everything.
The bell has one joke. It screams, and everyone suddenly remembers they have legs.
Cartography jokes always depend on scale.
I had a joke about north, but it went over everyone's head.
A bad map joke has no direction and still takes too long.
I folded a joke once and could never find the punchline again.
The compass laughed at me. It only does that in circles.
I know a road joke, but it wanders before getting anywhere.
My ink joke dried up before I finished it.
A map walked into the market and immediately got unfolded by gossip.
I drew a joke in the margins. It is not to scale.
The best landmark joke is obvious once you are already lost.
I told a coastline joke, but it kept changing shape.
A compass joke only points one way, and somehow still misses.
I mapped the punchline, then took the scenic route.
My road joke has several branches and one regrettable shortcut.
I would explain the joke, but then we would need a legend.
